title: Bound NumPy dataset digest allocations to the sampled prefix
body:
### Related Issues/PRs No linked issue. ### What changes are proposed in this pull request? `compute_numpy_digest` hashes at most 10,000 elements, but currently calls `array.flatten()` first. That allocates and copies the entire array, including all elements the digest will discard. Large training arrays and non-contiguous views therefore incur unnecessary input-sized memory and copy costs during dataset tracking. Slice the array's flat iterator directly. This selects the same C-order prefix while allocating only the sampled elements. Array shapes, dictionary-key order, target hashing and the existing TypeError fallback remain unchanged. A local five-repetition benchmark measured peak traced allocations for digest computation after warming imports; input allocation is excluded: | Float64 elements | Layout | Before peak bytes | After peak bytes | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | 10,000 | Contiguous | 241,016 | 240,920 | | 1,000,000 | Contiguous | 8,161,016 | 240,920 | | 1,000,000 | Transposed | 8,161,016 | 240,920 | | 4,000,000 | Contiguous | 32,161,016 | 240,920 | | 4,000,000 | Transposed | 32,161,016 | 240,920 | All benchmark digests match before and after. These measurements isolate fingerprint computation on one machine; they are not total model-training memory or end-to-end speed claims. Arrays already within the sampled prefix have approximately the same allocation footprint. ### How is this PR tested? - [x] Existing unit/integration tests - [x] New unit/integration tests - [x] Manual tests The eleven new tests have 3 failing allocation checks and 8 passing fingerprint controls on the baseline. With the fix, `pytest -p pytest_mock -p pytest_timeout tests/data/test_numpy_digest_memory.py tests/data/test_numpy_dataset.py -q` passes all 28 tests. The allocation checks use 16 MB contiguous/transposed/reversed arrays and a 2 MB upper bound. Fingerprint controls cover C and Fortran layouts, transposed and negative-stride views, object arrays, empty/scalar arrays, named features and targets. The existing native `NumpyDataset` tests retain their known digest and conversion assertions. Pinned Ruff, Clint, character normalization and `git diff --check` pass. The full repository suite was not run. Full pre-commit initialization remains blocked by npm's `EALLOWGIT` restriction while preparing the Prettier environment; Python checks were run directly. ### Does this PR require documentation update? - [x] No. ### Does this PR require updating the [MLflow Skills](https://github.com/mlflow/skills) repository? - [x] No. ### Release Notes #### Is this a user-facing change? - [x] Yes. Avoid copying entire NumPy datasets when computing a digest of their sampled prefix. #### What component(s), interfaces, languages, and integrations does this PR affect? Components - [x] `area/tracking`: Tracking Service, tracking client APIs, autologging #### How should the PR be classified in the release notes? Choose one: - [x] `rn/bug-fix` - A user-facing bug fix worth mentioning in the release notes #### Is this PR a critical bugfix or security fix that should go into the next patch release?
What is a minor/patch release? - Minor release: a release that increments the second part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.3.0). Minor releases are expected to contain larger changes, such as new features and improvements. Non-critical bug fixes and doc updates can be included as well. By default, your PR should target the next minor release. - Patch release: a release that increments the third part of the version number (e.g., 1.2.0 -> 1.2.1). Patch releases are typically only performed when there has been a major regression or bug in the latest release. For the sake of stability, your PR should not be included in a patch release unless it is a critical fix, or if the risk level of your PR is exceedingly low.
- [ ] This PR is critical and needs to be in the next patch release - [x] This PR can wait for the next minor release
